originalTitle: Rastafarians in Kenya fail in bid to get cannabis legalised for religious purposes
title: Big News from Kenya! Talking About a Special Plant!
content:
Hello, Super Friends!

Hello, hello, my amazing news explorers! It's your friend, Reporting Rhino, zooming in from our wonderful continent of Africa! Today, we have a very interesting story from a sunny country called Kenya. It's about some special people, a special plant, and some very big talks! Sometimes, grown-ups go to a special place called a 'court'. A court is where wise judges help decide what is fair and what rules everyone should follow. Imagine it like a giant classroom where people discuss big important things for the whole country. Our story today is about a group of people called Rastafarians. They are wonderful people who love peace, music, and living very close to nature. They believe in kindness and community.

Who Are the Rastafarians?

Imagine people who have special hairstyles called 'dreadlocks'. These long, beautiful locks are part of their identity and culture. Rastafarians often wear colorful clothes, especially red, green, and gold, which have special meanings for them. They believe in living simply and being grateful for everything around them. Their faith is about loving God and loving each other. They often listen to special music called Reggae, which sends messages of peace and happiness all around the world. Did you know? Reggae music, made famous by Bob Marley, came from Jamaica! Many Rastafarians live there, but you can find them all over the world, including right here in Africa!

The Special Plant: Cannabis

Now, let's talk about a plant. It's called 'cannabis'. You know how we have many plants around us, like maize, beans, or beautiful flowers? Well, cannabis is also a plant that grows from the ground. For the Rastafarians, this cannabis plant is very special. It's not just any plant for them. They see it as a holy herb, something that helps them connect with their God and think deeply during their prayers and meditations. They believe it helps them to be calm, to think clearly, and to understand their faith better. It's like a special tool for their religious practices, much like how some people use special candles or books for their prayers. Did you know? Plants are amazing! They give us oxygen to breathe and food to eat. Some plants are used for medicine, and some for making clothes, like cotton!

Going to Court for Their Faith

So, the Rastafarians in Kenya had a big wish. They wanted to be able to use this special cannabis plant for their religious ceremonies without getting into trouble. They believe it's their right to practice their religion fully. So, they went to the court. They bravely asked the wise judges to understand their needs. They explained that for them, using cannabis is not about fun, but about serious prayer and connecting with their faith. They wanted the judges to say 'yes', that it was okay for them. They shared their hearts and explained why this plant is so important to their way of life and worship. They hoped the judges would see things from their point of view and let them use the plant for their spiritual reasons.

What Did the Judges Say?

The judges listened very carefully to everything the Rastafarians said. They thought about it for a long, long time. It’s a big decision, you see, because the rules in Kenya say that cannabis is not allowed for everyone right now. After much thought, the judges made their decision. They said 'No, not right now.' They explained that the current laws in Kenya do not allow the use of cannabis, even for religious reasons. So, their wish was not granted this time. It can be sad when you don't get what you wish for, but the judges had an even bigger message to share. And that message is very, very important for all of Kenya! Did you know? Judges often wear special robes and sometimes even wigs in some countries! They do this to show they are fair and serious about their work!

A Big National Talk!

Here’s the really exciting part, my young news reporters! Even though the judges said 'no' for now, they also said something wonderful. They said, 'Kenya needs to have a very big talk about this plant!' Imagine the whole country of Kenya sitting down together, like a super-sized family meeting. This is what the judges called a 'national debate'. A 'debate' means many people will talk, share their ideas, and listen to each other about cannabis. They want people from all over Kenya – grown-ups, community leaders, doctors, parents, and maybe even scientists – to share their thoughts and feelings about the cannabis plant. Should the rules change? Should it be allowed for some reasons? These are the big questions! This means that the judges understood that this is a very important topic. They know that many people have different ideas about the plant, and that it's important to hear everyone's voice before making new rules. Did you know? Kenya is a beautiful country in East Africa, famous for its amazing wildlife like lions, elephants, and giraffes! It has stunning national parks and reserves!

What Happens Next?

So, what does this mean for Kenya? It means that the conversation about cannabis is not over. It has just begun in a bigger way! The court has asked the whole country to think and talk about it. It’s like when you and your friends want to decide on a new game to play. You all talk about the pros and cons, right? That’s what Kenya needs to do about this plant. Everyone will share their thoughts and ideas. This is a chance for people to learn more, to understand different points of view, and to think about what is best for everyone in Kenya. Maybe, after these big talks, the rules about cannabis might change one day. Or maybe they will stay the same. Only time, and good talking, will tell!

Learning to Talk and Listen

This story from Kenya teaches us something very important, my young friends. It teaches us about talking and listening. Even when people don't agree, it's super important to talk respectfully and listen to each other's ideas. The Rastafarians bravely spoke about their beliefs. The judges listened and made a decision based on current rules, but then asked for more discussion. This is how fair countries work – everyone gets a chance to be heard. So, let’s all remember to talk kindly, listen carefully, and keep learning new things every day! That's all for today from Reporting Rhino! Keep exploring, keep learning, and keep being awesome! Goodbye for now!
summary: Rastafarians in Kenya asked a court if they could use a special plant called cannabis for their religion, but the judges said no for now and asked the whole country to have a big talk about the plant instead.
whyMatters: This story is important because it shows that even big countries need to talk and listen to different people's ideas to decide what rules are fair for everyone, especially when it comes to things like religion and plants.

originalTitle: Prominent Moroccan journalist Ali Lmrabet released from custody
title: Happy News from Morocco: Our Friend Ali is Free!
content:
Hey there, amazing kids of Africa! Your friendly news reporter is here with some wonderful and happy news from a beautiful country called Morocco! Imagine a place with sunny beaches, colourful markets, and towering mountains – that's Morocco! Today, we have some special news about a very brave person named Ali Lmrabet. He is a journalist, which means he is a super storyteller who tells *real* stories about what's happening in the world. And guess what? He was held for a little while, but now he is free! Yes, you heard that right, Ali Lmrabet is back with his family, and that is fantastic news for everyone who loves hearing important stories.

Who is Ali Lmrabet?

Ali Lmrabet is like a super detective, but instead of solving mysteries, he finds out all the important news and then shares it with everyone! He writes about things happening in Morocco, his home country. He wants all the grown-ups and even the children to know what's going on so they can understand their world better. *Did you know?* A journalist is like a storyteller for real life! They ask questions, listen to answers, and then write or speak about what they find. They help us learn new things every day! Ali Lmrabet loves to tell true stories, even if they are sometimes a bit tricky. He believes it's important for everyone to hear all sides of a story, so they can think for themselves. He is a very important person because he helps people understand their country.

Why Was Ali Held?

Sometimes, when people tell very important stories, especially stories about how things could be better or things that powerful grown-ups might not want to hear, it can make those grown-ups feel a little nervous. It’s a bit like when you share an idea in class, and maybe not everyone agrees with you, or someone might even try to stop you from talking. Ali Lmrabet was telling stories that some people in charge didn't like very much. Because of this, he was asked to stop, and then he was held for a short time. It wasn't fair, and it made many people sad. But the most important part is that now he is free! He can go back to being with his loved ones and maybe even continue to tell his important stories.

Why is it Important to Tell Stories?

Imagine if no one told you what was happening in your school, or your town, or your country. How would you know if something important was happening? How would you know about new rules or exciting events? Journalists like Ali Lmrabet help us understand the world around us. They help us learn new things and think about how we can make our communities even better. It's super, super important for everyone to be able to share their thoughts and tell their stories, without being afraid. This special right is called "freedom of speech." *Did you know?* Freedom of speech means you can share your ideas, your opinions, and your stories with others without fear of getting into trouble. It's like having a super big voice that everyone can hear! It helps us all learn and grow together.

What is Morocco Like?

Morocco is a truly magical country in North Africa. It's known for its bright, sunny skies and its long, beautiful coastlines along the Atlantic Ocean and the Mediterranean Sea. The capital city is Rabat, but many people know Casablanca, which is a very big city! Morocco is famous for its delicious food, like couscous and tagine, and its colourful, bustling markets called souks, where you can find all sorts of treasures. People there are often very friendly and welcoming. *Did you know?* Morocco is home to parts of the Sahara Desert, one of the biggest and hottest deserts in the world! Imagine riding a camel over huge sand dunes, just like in the movies! It's a land full of amazing adventures.

What About Other Storytellers?

The news also tells us that sometimes other people who share their ideas might face difficulties too. For example, there was also a rapper who shares his thoughts through music and rhymes! A rapper is someone who tells stories and expresses feelings using cool beats and rhythmic words. It's like poetry set to music! Sometimes, even when people sing songs or make music that talks about real life, it can make some powerful grown-ups nervous. Just like with journalists, it's important for musicians to be able to share their art and their messages freely.

What are "Activists"?

The news mentions some special people called "activists." Who are they? Activists are like real-life superheroes! They are people who really, really care about making things fair and good for everyone. They work hard to make sure people can speak freely and that everyone is treated kindly and with respect. When Ali Lmrabet was held, these activists spoke up very loudly. They said, "Hey! This is not fair! Ali should be free to tell his stories!" They wrote letters, they talked to many people, and they helped make sure Ali could come home. They are very brave and helpful people!

Why Does This Matter to You?

This news might seem like it's happening far away, but it's important for all of us, even for amazing kids like you. It reminds us that everyone has a voice. Even you! When you share your ideas in class, or tell your parents what you think, or draw a picture that shows how you feel, you are using your voice. We want everyone in the world, big or small, to feel safe and happy to share their thoughts and stories. When people like Ali Lmrabet are free to tell their stories, it means more true stories can be told, and that helps everyone learn, understand, and grow. It helps us build a kinder, fairer world.

A Message of Hope!

So, remember this happy news: Ali Lmrabet is free! It's a wonderful step towards making sure everyone in Morocco, and all over Africa, can share their stories and their ideas without fear. Let's keep hoping for a world where everyone's voice is heard, cherished, and celebrated! That's all for today from your friendly African news reporter! Keep being amazing, keep asking questions, and keep sharing your wonderful ideas!
summary: Moroccan journalist Ali Lmrabet, a brave storyteller, has been released from custody, bringing happy news for those who believe in sharing ideas and stories freely.
whyMatters: It matters because it shows that even when people face challenges for speaking up, their freedom to tell stories is important and helps everyone learn and understand the world better.
